title: QPS drift lab scrub — hypothesis log and test runs (2025-10-09)
content:
Summary:
Quick sync notes from the QPS drift lab scrub on 2025-10-09. Goal: triage a steady ~8-12% drop in observed QPS on prod-like serving pools over the last three weeks, identify reproducible failure mode in bench, and land a mitigation plan (short term) + fix (medium term).

Attendees:
- Avery Chen (owner)
- Ravi Menon (batcher/rt)
- Sana Iqbal (observability)
- Elena Morales (perf tooling)
- Notes: ad-hoc input from oncall (Slack threads linked in artifacts)

Quick TL;DR findings:
- Reproducible in bench when we add realistic token distribution (mix of short/long sequences) + periodic small bursts (microbursts). Baseline steady-state no-burst tests did not show the same degradation.
- Primary symptom: increased per-request CPU jitter on CPU proxy and longer waiting time in the request prequeue (batcher wait). p95 latency up ~15% for 128-token avg workloads; p99 spikes tied to K/V cache evictions.
- Two working hypotheses: (H1) batching heuristics are over-optimizing for cost (increasing batch delay under certain arrival patterns), (H2) KV cache churn due to slightly different input prefixes increasing cache misses -> more host<->device transfers. Likely both contribute.

Test matrix ran today (details in gs export):
- env: bench-xlarge-prodlike (A10G), 32 workers, same model version v2.3.1 (int8 quant)
- workload profiles: steady-1k qps fixed, mixed-1k qps (60% short 16-32 tok, 30% mid 128 tok, 10% long 512 tok), bursty (900 qps steady + 3x microburst every 60s lasting 6s)
- batcher params varied: max_batch=1024, max_latency_ms=[2,6,12], prefer_latency=true/false, batch_cutoff=0.85
- KV cache variants: warm (cold start warmed for 5m), cold (evict after every request), adaptive-evict (current prod candidate)

Selected results (from latest run):
- mixed-1k / prefer_latency=false / max_latency=6ms / adaptive-evict -> QPS down 9% vs baseline (steady workload). p95 latency +14%, p99 +36% with 3x isolated spike events per 60s aligning with microbursts.
- bursty / prefer_latency=true / max_latency=2ms / warm -> QPS stable but cost rises (GPU util up 6%), p99 still shows occasional spikes but lower frequency.
- cold KV / any batcher config -> p99 latency increased dramatically (up to 2.8x) and overall QPS reduced by 20% in mixed workloads.

Observability notes (Sana):
- Traces show that when the microburst arrives, many requests queue and the batcher suddenly creates a large batch which then causes longer kernel setup time (we observed extra 10-30ms for kernel launch after a large contiguous batch).
- CPU proxy time metric (proxy_cpu_ms) shows bimodal distribution in degraded runs; tail corresponds to times when host-side copying and KV eviction handlers run.
- New metric to add: kv-evict-rate and batcher-coalesce-events (count of large batch formations in last 60s).

Hypothesis deep-dive:
- H1 (batcher heuristics): prefer_latency=false (current shipped default for many customers to reduce token cost) allows the batcher to wait longer to fill batches. Under mixed/bursty traffic that leads to larger, less predictable batches and longer GPU kernel prep time. Combined with microbursts this pushes p99 higher.
- H2 (KV cache churn): small shifts in input prefixes (recent customer rollout produced more variant prompts) increased KV miss rate by ~4% in bench which cascades into more host<->device memory copies; this is expensive on A10G for large sequence lengths.
- Combined mode: large batches + heavier KV activity -> contention in GPU memory bus and increase in proxy processing time.

Immediate action items (short term, owners):
- (Avery) Backfill last 30 days of production kv-miss-rate and batch-size histograms; compare against bench distribution (due EOD 2025-10-10).
- (Ravi) Run targeted bench where we force prefer_latency=true for a canary pool to verify swap reduces p99 spikes (two configs: prefer_latency=true with max_latency=2ms and with 6ms) (due 2025-10-11).
- (Sana) Add kv-evict-rate and batcher-coalesce-events to Grafana dashboards and set a provisional alert threshold (kv-evict-rate > 1% sustained and batcher-coalesce-events > 5/min) (due 2025-10-12).
- (Elena) Capture kernel-launch traces and host<->device memcpy times for the large-batch scenario; annotate bench exports (gs) (due 2025-10-12).
- (All) Draft a short customer-facing blurb about investigating a performance regression and temporary guidance: suggest prefer_latency=true for latency-sensitive routes (Avery to draft, due 2025-10-13).

Medium-term mitigation candidates:
- Make batcher heuristics adaptive to microburst patterns (incorporate recent inter-arrival statistics to decide when to lower max_latency).
- Add KV cache admission policy that prioritizes long-seq requests (so short requests don't evict entries needed by long requests) or size-aware eviction.
- Improve kernel launch pipeline: pre-allocate workspace for predicted max-batch-size to reduce dynamic allocation penalty.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much of the regression is directly customer-visible (many routes are internal tooling vs customer traffic)? Need route-level breakdown.
- Are specific model variants showing worse sensitivity (we only tested v2.3.1 int8 so far)? Schedule tests on fp16 and v2.2.
- Could recent infra framerates (driver 542.xx update rolled 2025-09-29) be contributing? Need to correlate with driver upgrades across pools.

Notes-to-self / rough commands run today:
- bench runner: ./bench/run.py --profile mixed-1k --workers 32 --model v2.3.1 --quant int8 --burst-pattern microburst60 --batcher-prefers-latency false --max-latency-ms 6
- perf export: gsutil cp /tmp/bench-2025-10-09.tgz gs://bench-exports/qps-drift/oct09/
- small check: jq '.[].metrics | {qps,p95,p99}' /tmp/bench-summary.json > /tmp/qps-snapshot.json

References / links in artifacts: bench export, PR GH-PR-2345 (batcher metrics changes), JIRA-INF-879 (prod regression ticket), confluence page with playback traces.

Next sync:
- Quick follow-up standup Mon 2025-10-13 10:00 PDT to review initial canary results and dashboards. If prefer_latency=true removes p99 spikes without unacceptable cost, plan short-term guided rollback for sensitive routes and open a longer RFC for adaptive batching and KV admission.

Free-form brainstorming notes (messy):
- Could we prioritize KV entries by TTL + use lightweight LRU sharding to reduce global eviction storms?
- Consider per-route batcher profile overrides so that known bursty routes get smaller max_latency.
- Add a cheap probabilistic sampler that forces a tiny fraction of requests to bypass the KV cache to help measure true miss cost in production without full bench.

End of notes.
